Add a VPN profile in Profiles by importing a v2raytun link, configuration file, or QR code.
 Control logic - the app supports three main operating modes - VPN, Tor, and VPN + Tor. Each mode is controlled by a whole-device or proxy routing scenario. Scenarios are built from app and web-address rules.
 The whole-device scenario sends all outgoing traffic through the tunnel. The proxy scenario applies routing rules to selected apps; web-address rules operate within the active scenario.
Additional modules: Firewall, Tor, I2P, and DNS filtering. They can run alongside any app mode or independently.
“Apply scenarios atomically”: when enabled, VPN and Tor scenarios apply automatically without extra prompts; when disabled, every scenario change requires confirmation. VPN rules for Wi-Fi/mobile networks are always applied atomically.
Supported protocols: VLESS, VMess, Hysteria2, WireGuard, AmneziaWG, Trojan, Shadowsocks, Naive, TUIC, and AnyTLS.
FoxHole DB downloads only the data sets required by enabled features.
All settings and profiles are stored locally in encrypted form. Encryption keys are protected by Android Keystore. Security can additionally require a FoxHole Guard PIN or system biometrics.
The app-monitoring module records installations and removals. Quarantine blocks new apps’ network access until user approval; it is active while a tunnel or the firewall is running.

The “whole device” scenario sends all OS network traffic through the VPN tunnel (routing rules for individual apps are ignored in this mode). The proxy scenario supports two modes: “selected apps only” and “all except selected apps” (routing rules apply). Configure scenarios under Routing → App Rules. VPN and Tor scenarios are configured separately, but compatibility restrictions apply: “whole-device VPN + Tor for selected apps” is supported; the reverse configuration is not. Local network proxy settings are in the Extras section.

FoxHole Guard does not currently support routing Tor inside a VPN tunnel over UDP-based VPN protocols. To run Tor inside a VPN, use a TCP-based protocol, or run Tor alongside an active VPN connection. Tor operates exclusively over TCP, so UDP traffic such as VoIP calls is not routed through Tor; HTTP/HTTPS streaming is possible but may be slow. When Tor is routed through a VPN, your internet provider sees only the VPN connection, but the VPN provider may see a connection to a Tor entry node or bridge and its associated metadata. The MODE button on the Home screen switches between VPN / VPN + Tor / Tor. If direct Tor connections are blocked, enable bridges in Tor settings; the bridge list is downloaded from FoxHole DB through a FoxHole Team mirror or directly from Tor Project servers.

A Smart VPN profile combines several VPN protocols for one server into a single list for quick switching and connection testing.
Legend|T connection time; P server ping; L latency
Latency colors|up to 150 ms, 151–300 ms, 301–600 ms, over 600 ms
You can test all protocols available in the subscription; this blocks all device traffic, switches the app to whole-device VPN mode, measures three parameters, and restores the last active connection. The ★ icon marks the best connections from the test results.

Traffic routing rules for apps and web resources are applied atomically.
In the “whole device” scenario, app routing rules are ignored but remain saved in the configuration. They apply only in the proxy scenario, where routing for VPN and Tor is configured separately and traffic from specified apps can be sent through the tunnel or excluded from it.
Blocking network access for apps works while a VPN/Tor tunnel is active or the firewall is enabled.
Important: the firewall started by I2P in transparent mode does not apply general routing rules—blocking and DNS interception are disabled, and only .i2p domain traffic is routed.

The Main Journal records FoxHole Guard events: module starts and stops, state changes, and system events. The Network Journal records individual network connections (timestamp, app, protocol, destination country, and data volume). The Security Journal stores FoxHole Sentinel events, including app changes and network anomalies. All journals are stored locally in encrypted form and are never sent to external servers.

The Statistics module collects traffic, active-session, and DNS-query metrics locally. It lets you analyze VPN profiles, apps, DNS blocks, firewall events, and Tor/I2P networks over a selected period. The module is disabled by default. When enabled, you can configure the collection interval, retention period, and individual metrics. Data is aggregated by day, week, and month and is stored only on the device.

The local firewall blocks network access for selected apps. Its rules apply while a supported tunnel is active or while the firewall module runs independently. With Quarantine enabled (which requires the firewall or one of the primary operating modes), newly installed apps are denied internet access by default until you explicitly allow them. Manage it under Settings → Firewall → Module Settings.

The FoxHole Guard tile in Android Quick Settings lets you turn the connection on or off without opening the app. Starting from the tile uses the most recently selected operating mode from the Home screen.
Block traffic when the connection drops

Kill Switch uses Android’s system “Block connections without VPN” mechanism. If the VPN connection drops, the operating system blocks all network traffic and prevents data from leaking to the open network. Configure it in the device’s system VPN settings.

Settings → Application → Encryption and lock. This section exports FoxHole Guard profiles and transferable settings to an encrypted (AES) backup file. Important: profiles may contain credentials such as VPN accounts or subscriptions, so store the backup file and its decryption password separately. A forgotten password cannot be recovered.\nDuring restore (import), the app applies profiles and transferable settings but retains this device’s local values: the FoxHole Guard PIN, update token, OS permissions (Usage Access), generated local-proxy passwords, and local FoxHole Sentinel databases. The backup contents are shown for confirmation before import. \nThe same section provides selective clearing of journals, statistics, and profiles, as well as a complete and irreversible Factory Reset.

DNS settings apply to traffic inside supported tunnels. When “Device DNS protection” is enabled, FoxHole Guard starts a local DNS resolver, allowing DNS filtering to work even without an active VPN or Tor connection. Filter lists are downloaded from FoxHole DB. Configured exclusions send DNS requests from specified apps or domains to the device’s system DNS servers.

Limitations: DNS filtering does not apply to WireGuard or AmneziaWG (WireGuard uses the DNS specified by its profile; AmneziaWG currently does not support DNS interception).

DNS monitoring: the app tracks the system DNS server configuration. A sudden complete replacement of the current server set is recorded in the Security Journal as a potential indicator of compromise (DNS hijacking).

This feature binds a specific VPN profile to a Wi-Fi or mobile network. When the network interface changes, FoxHole Guard sends a push notification suggesting that you activate the profile or automatically connects the selected VPN profile.

The built-in proxy server routes traffic from other devices on the local Wi-Fi network through an active VPN or Tor tunnel on your device using SOCKS5 or HTTP.\nSecurity requirement: authentication for the local proxy is mandatory. The server cannot start with an empty password.\nImportant: FoxHole Guard does not encrypt traffic between the client device and your phone. Use this feature only on trusted local networks.

Long-press a saved VPN profile to open its management actions: select, rename, edit, or delete. To save or share a saved VPN profile, select it and use the controls below. Sharing through a QR code is available for a single configuration and v2raytun subscriptions. The “+” button in VPN Profiles creates a new configuration from a blank template with a selectable protocol type.\nIn a Smart profile, each protocol is stored as an isolated entry and configured independently.\nSecurity: connections without certificate verification (Insecure TLS/AllowInsecure) require explicit user confirmation; this permission is stored locally only for the profile being edited.

Supported import formats are a URI copied to the clipboard, a configuration file, and a scanned QR code. When a subscription profile in v2raytun format is added, FoxHole Guard updates it automatically before connecting. Long-press START to update the subscription manually without connecting. Multi-select mode lets you select several profiles for batch export to a file. A single profile or protocol can be shared as a URI or QR code.

The Security section controls access to the app through a FoxHole Guard PIN or system biometrics.
All profiles and settings are stored locally in encrypted form by default; encryption keys are generated and protected by hardware-backed Android Keystore. 
System biometrics serve as an authentication gate and do not re-encrypt the data. When a FoxHole Guard PIN is used, biometric sign-in asks Keystore for a separate key that requires authentication for every operation and unlocks the primary PIN-protected keybox. 
The Security Journal is encrypted with a separate key and protected by a cryptographic hash chain. Biometrics do not add another encryption layer to the journal: after successful sign-in, the app decrypts the journal and verifies the chain against its pinned checkpoint. Sensitive data is never sent to FoxHole Team infrastructure servers.

FoxHole Sentinel is a behavioral-analysis module based on OS and network metadata. It does not inspect traffic payloads and is not an antivirus. FoxHole Sentinel signals indicate potentially malicious anomalies but do not guarantee that malicious code is present.
App analysis: the installation source and requested privileges are checked against built-in security lists (Security IOCs). Indicators of compromise, including stalkerware IOCs, are updated through FoxHole DB. The baseline stalkerware indicator list is based on AssoEchap/stalkerware-indicators (CC-BY-4.0).
Network analysis: the traffic detector compares aggregate network-activity windows minute by minute. Signals that require analysis of individual apps’ background traffic also use local OS statistics.
When a PIN and event monitoring are enabled, FoxHole Sentinel records app installations and removals, the background service heartbeat, and suspicious monitoring gaps in a cryptographically protected hash-chained journal.
Operating modes: Economy does not use a permanent foreground service; Reinforced runs a persistent service with a system notification, improving reliability at the cost of higher battery use. 
Limitations: force-stopping the app in Android settings pauses monitoring. FoxHole Sentinel cannot prevent user actions, processes with root privileges, or clearing app data through the system.

FoxHole DB is the app’s artifact repository and contains five data sets: DNS filter lists, Tor bridges, IOC lists (FoxHole Sentinel), IP geodatabases, and TLS fingerprint tables. The app downloads only the data sets required by enabled features. Every artifact is cryptographically verified before it is applied atomically. Settings → Updates shows FoxHole DB synchronization status and lets you start an update manually or configure an automatic schedule.

Enabling transit routing helps increase the network’s overall throughput and resilience.\n\nAll transit traffic is encapsulated and end-to-end encrypted; your device acts only as an intermediate router, not as the initiator or final recipient of the data. The confidentiality of user traffic is fully preserved, and relay mode can be disabled at any time.

The FoxHole Guard software kill switch does not replace the system protection
Enable “Block connections without VPN” in system settings

Differences between the emergency blocking mechanisms (Kill Switch):

1. The app’s software Kill Switch blocks network connections if the VPN tunnel drops while FoxHole Guard is running. Protection ends if the OS removes the process from memory.

2. Android’s system Kill Switch (“Block connections without VPN”) blocks every interface at the OS level regardless of whether the app process is running.

Using both mechanisms together is recommended for maximum protection.
